translation.english_text: (Garudan Publishing House.)
Sir! Editor sir!

Don't call me that! An editor—the author of books of knowledge—a beautiful craftsman of words—the leader of suffering workers—you don't know the terrible secrets hidden behind these glittering silk curtains, brother! You don't know.
Paranthama!
Not Paranthaman—a terrifying beast, a beast! No longer a beast—I have become a human being. Only today have I become human.
What are you saying, man, like someone who's gone mad?
Gone mad? The madness that had possessed me has only now cleared, because of my akka.
Right. Looks as though akka has preached to you. Looks as though you've really improved.

Don't say anything about akka—she is my deity. The deity who opened the doors of my heart that had been shut! The jewel of womanhood who showed a lamp of light on my dark path. When I was about to fall into the pit of disgrace, she gave me a final breath and commanded me: 'Look, you worthless man devoid of character. How many flower-faced women have been crushed under your footsteps along the path you have walked—those left without direction, those led astray, those struggling in the streets—how many are there? Traitor, look back!' The deity who reformed me with that command is my beloved sister. She alone is the living deity before my eyes. Garuda, I walked only on an evil path. So did you, so did you. You too reform yourself—look back, my friend—look back!
notes: The printed phrase is `பண்பு கெட்ட வீணனே`; the translation preserves its direct condemnation without altering the Tamil source.

translation.english_text: Oh, go on!
You won't be able to look back so easily. You're an elephant.
Paranthama, what is this bad idea that has suddenly come over you?

A good sense has come to me, you destroyer—don't push me into your net any longer. Paranthaman has changed his path. He is going to seek atonement for the injustices he committed. Akka! Your younger brother is about to enter immediately upon a good deed. I am going to reunite Pandiyan and Kumudha and rejoice. I am going to ask Bama's forgiveness.
Paranthama!
I'm leaving. Don't call me.
I'll come with you too.
Come, brother, come. If you stay here, you'll be ruined too.
(The boy writes.)
Hey, what is this, da?
Look back.
('Garudan Publishing House' appears as 'Thief Publishing House.')
notes: The source uses the visual wordplay `கருடன் பதிப்பகம் - திருடன் பதிப்பகமாக்கப்படுகிறது`; it is retained as a written/visual gag rather than assigned to a speaker.
